data.title: Tesla Sets Next-Gen Roadster Reveal for October 1 – ‘Go For Launch’
data.description:
Tesla has finally announced the launch date of the next-gen Roadster. The company will hold a reveal event on October 1 and has teased a much-talked-about feature.

After a decade of releasing every product except the Roadster reboot, Tesla has finally shared a date to take the wraps off the iconic car. The company shared a teaser on X, indicating fans can mark October 1 on their calendar for the unveiling.

 

The teaser image above also stoked rumours that the refreshed Roadster will debut with cold-gas thrusters borrowed from sister company SpaceX. If reports from The Information are correct, the thrusters will allow the Roadster to temporarily lift off the ground. Tesla is reportedly developing two versions, with one able to take to fly and another that sticks to the ground. Both will be built at Giga Texas.

According to the same report, the flying Roadster will cost a pretty penny, possibly over a million dollars. However, the car is claimed to be so powerful that the demo unit would be operated remotely by someone outside the car to protect their eardrums. Whatever the final price, the Roadster is a halo product; hence, it will have a limited production run.

Tesla has updated its website with a countdown timer to the October 1 debut, and along with the post on X, Tesla already started sending out invitations to reservations holders, confirming the event will take place in Waco, Texas.

Despite taking time out to develop a variety of products, from EVs to AI to robotics, Tesla has continued to hype the Roadster. CEO Elon Musk boasted the supercar will incorporate a SpaceX package, referring to the thrusters. VP of Engineering Lars Moravy claimed the Roadster is the “last, best driver’s car” before autonomous vehicles flood the roads. Chief Designer Franz von Holzhausen stated last month that the car was getting close to its big reveal.

data.title: The Boring Company files permits for another tunnel near Giga Texas
data.description:
The Boring Company has filed site plans for a new tunnel project running beneath the Colorado River near Giga Texas.

Called the Tesla Colorado River Tunnel, the project would see The Boring Company construct a single-lane connector tunnel. The tunnel would go under the Colorado River and connect with 1000-1/2 Fallwell Lane.

However, the project proposal does not specify a length at this time.

This is the second time that The Boring Company has proposed a tunnelling project adjacent to Giga Texas.

The last proposal for the Colorado River Connector Tunnel was intended as a private access tunnel and did not move forward.

This latest application appears to update the 2022 plan, with similar engineering plans and drawings.

If those remain the plan, the tunnel would stretch roughly 2 miles point to point.

In their proposal, the proponent, TBC Project Development, did not disclose other details, including what the tunnel would be used for and whether Tesla plans future development on the River Road site.

data.title: Tesla Oasis Supercharger serves 6,038 drivers on Labor Day weekend
data.description:
Tesla’s massive Oasis Supercharger in Lost Hills, California, faced one of its busiest tests yet over the Labor Day long weekend, and handled the holiday rush without a single charging queue.

According to Tesla Charging, drivers completed 6,038 charging sessions across the site’s 164 stalls over four days. That works out to more than 1,500 sessions per day, or an average of 9.2 sessions per stall over the long weekend. Traffic peaked on Labor Day, when each stall averaged 11.2 sessions, yet Tesla reported “zero waiters.”

At the busiest point of the weekend, 116 vehicles were plugged in simultaneously, drawing a combined 11.4 megawatts (MW) of power. Max de Zegher, Tesla’s Director of Charging for North America, shared the figure on X, adding, “All electrical loads will eventually transition to solar + storage. The giant fusion reactor in the sky is free.”

The site’s solar installation generated 7 MW of power during the holiday, helping support thousands of charging stops along Interstate 5, one of California’s busiest travel corridors.

Tesla partially opened Oasis in July 2025 with 84 stalls before completing the full 164-stall facility later that year. The final layout includes 12 pull-through stalls for vehicles towing trailers, along with restrooms, a driver lounge and outdoor seating areas.

Oasis is designed as a majority off-grid charging station, pairing an 11 MW solar farm with 10 Tesla Megapacks. The battery system can store a combined 39 megawatt-hours (MWh) of energy, allowing electricity collected during the day to continue powering chargers after sunset or during periods of heavy demand.

data.title: Tesla unveils European Semi with cameras for side mirrors, deliveries start next year
data.description:
Tesla has officially unveiled the European version of the Semi, revealing a truck adapted for the region’s roads and regulations ahead of deliveries beginning in 2027.

When it comes to stats, the European Semi offers a different package from its North American counterpart, with an estimated range of 550 kilometres (342 miles). That is well below the 804 km (500-mile) range of the Long Range Semi in the U.S., although the difference can likely be attributed, at least in part, to the heavier loads carried in Europe.

Tesla’s European estimate is based on a total combination weight of 40 tonnes, while the U.S. estimate is based on a fully loaded Semi at 82,000 lbs, or about 37.2 tonnes.

Tesla says its fast-charging system can add up to 60 per cent of the truck’s range in 30 minutes, potentially returning about 330 km of driving range during a typical rest stop.

Power output is listed at up to 800 kW, while an electric power take-off system, or ePTO, can supply up to 25 kW for equipment attached to the truck.

European Semi Gets Several Design Changes

Although its overall shape remains familiar, the European model includes some noticeable differences from the Semi offered in North America. Traditional side mirrors have been removed and replaced by a camera-based system, helping reduce drag while also meeting the needs of narrower European roads.

The front end has also been updated with slightly different headlights with no full-length lightbar, and no amber turn signals or amber lights above the cab. The European version is also missing black trim behind the cab.

Europe will become the Semi’s first major market outside North America. However, Tesla has not yet announced pricing, confirmed which countries will receive the truck first, or provided more specific delivery dates beyond saying they will begin in 2027.

That information will likely come next week when Tesla officially debuts the European Semi at IAA Transportation in Hannover, Germany from September 15 through 20.

data.title: Tesla Rolls Out Widespread Supercharger Price Changes Across Canada
data.description:
Tesla has quietly changed Supercharger prices across Canada, leaving most drivers paying more than they were a day earlier.

A review of Supercharger prices across the country by Drive Tesla found that rates went up at more than 200 sites, while prices dropped at 65 locations, and 10 were unchanged.

For many Tesla owners, the increase is relatively small – typically between $0.01 and $0.03 per kWh. However, there are some notable exceptions, particularly in Alberta and Ontario. There were also significant increases for non-Tesla drivers who use the Supercharger network.

Higher Prices Across Alberta and Ontario

In Calgary and Edmonton, several Superchargers jumped from $0.51 to $0.57 per kWh. That includes Calgary’s 130 Avenue SE and Aviation Road NE locations, along with all three sites in Edmonton.

Drivers of non-Tesla EVs will see an even bigger increase at some locations. At Calgary’s 130 Avenue SE Supercharger, the rate climbed from $0.68 to $0.82 per kWh. Edmonton’s Currents Drive site made a similar jump, rising from $0.64 to $0.78.

Ontario followed the same general pattern. Many smaller cities saw Tesla rates rise by about two cents, while busier locations with peak pricing posted larger increases.

At Ottawa’s Campeau Drive Supercharger, the peak Tesla rate rose from $0.44 to $0.52 per kWh, although the off-peak rate remains $0.28. Burlington increased from $0.51 to $0.56 during peak hours, while Kitchener moved from $0.51 to $0.54. In both cases, the cheaper off-peak rate either stayed the same or came down slightly.

B.C. Is More of a Mixed Bag

British Columbia’s price changes were more mixed. Prices dropped at many highway and Interior locations, but rose at a number of busier urban Superchargers.

Campbell River, Tofino, Port Alberni, Kamloops and several other communities are now $0.03 per kWh cheaper for Tesla owners. Comox dropped from $0.24 to $0.22, while Williams Lake fell from $0.26 to $0.23.

Nanaimo’s original Supercharger at Woodgrove Centre also became cheaper, dropping from $0.29 to $0.26 during peak hours and from $0.21 to $0.19 off-peak. Across town, however, the newer North Island Highway site now has separate rates of $0.28 during peak hours and $0.22 off-peak.

Victoria’s Uptown Supercharger saw its peak rate increase slightly, from $0.33 to $0.35, while its $0.21 off-peak price stayed the same.

Enfield Climbs to $0.71 per kWh

One of the biggest increases was in Enfield, Nova Scotia, where Tesla’s peak rate rose from $0.64 to $0.71 per kWh. However, there is some relief for drivers charging outside the busiest hours, as the off-peak price dropped from $0.38 to $0.35.

Here is a list of notable price changes for Superchargers across Canada – remember to always check your app or the in-car navigation for the latest pricing in your area.

Let us know in the comments below if your local Superchargers increased or decreased in price.

data.title: The Boring Company Raises $3 billion in Latest Funding Round
data.description:
The Boring Company is the latest Elon Musk-owned entity to move forward with another funding round. The Boring Company announced this week it secured $3 billion in funding at an estimated $23 billion valuation.

The United Arab Emirates and affiliated investment entities led the round, with proceeds to develop more than 150 km (93 miles) of underground infrastructure in the country, including the previously announced Dubai Loop.

The Boring Company will also use some of the funding to hire more engineers, product, and operations staff to support its growing list of Loop projects in Nashville, Dubai, and Vegas.

The Boring Company signed a preliminary agreement with Dubai’s Roads and Transport Authority last year to build the Dubai Loop. So, this investment should mean significant construction is on the horizon for the planned 22 km route connecting the Dubai World Trade Centre to Business Bay.

An initial 6.4 km stretch will link Dubai Mall with the Dubai International Financial Centre.

In addition to the UAE and their investment entities, Human Capital, Vy Capital, Sequoia Capital, Valour Equity Partners, Baron Capital, Shamal Holding, Andreessen Horowitz and Temasek also participated in this funding round.

The company was last valued in 2022, when The Boring Company raised $675 million in a funding round that valued it at $5.7 billion.

data.title: Tesla inks massive 3 GWh Megapack deal with Zhero for Italy’s grid storage push
data.description:
Tesla Energy has added another major contract to its already impressive list of Megapack customers. The company has inked a massive deal with Zhero and H1 Holdings to supply high-performance Megapack energy storage batteries for projects in Italy and across multiple other sites.

The agreement covers a total capacity of 3 GWh, and all the projects will be located in Italy. It involves long-term purchase contracts which will help Zhero rely less on Italy’s regulatory support frameworks such as MACSE. Assured market access is crucial to Zhero’s attempt to transition from an ordinary project developer to an owner-operator.

Zhero will install Tesla’s Megapacks, starting with 200 MW of shovel-ready developments. The company currently has a pipeline of 1.5 GW of battery energy storage projects. It aims to capture a larger share of Italy’s commercial and industrial market.

Developers like Zhero will benefit from Tesla’s Megapack 3, which recently entered production in Texas. The latest upgrades reduce installation time and costs, increasing the brand’s global appeal.

Even before the latest version, Megapacks were the favorites of energy developers. Tesla signed a historic $5 billion deal with NatPower that will see more than 25 GWh worth of the batteries installed in the UK and Italy. In the Southern Hemisphere, a Megapack installation will power 44,000 homes in New Zealand. Another development in Queensland, Australia, will store up to 500 MWh of energy and supply the grid for up to two hours.

data.title: Canada’s ZEV Sales Jump 27% in Q2 2026, but Market Share Remains Flat
data.description:
Canada’s zero-emission vehicle (ZEV) market share remained virtually unchanged in the second quarter of 2026, even as overall new vehicle registrations surged nearly 40% from the first three months of the year.

According to data from Statistics Canada released this week, Canadians registered 547,673 new vehicles between April and June, up 37.7% from 397,601 in Q1 and 1.1% year-over-year. It was also the highest quarterly total since Q2 2019. ZEVs accounted for 58,811 registrations, giving them a 10.7% market share, compared with 10.8% in Q1.

Source: Statistics Canada

Battery-electric vehicles (BEVs) continued to make up most ZEV registrations, with 40,585 units representing 7.4% of the overall market, down slightly from 7.5% in Q1. Plug-in hybrids (PHEVs) added 18,226 registrations, holding steady at 3.3%.

Despite the flat quarter-over-quarter share, ZEV adoption remains well ahead of last year. ZEV registrations increased 26.7% from Q2 2025, when their market share stood at 8.6%. BEV registrations jumped 37.4% year-over-year, while PHEVs increased 8.0%.

The latest figures build on the strong EV sales rebound recorded in March. That followed the February launch of Canada’s new EV Affordability Program (EVAP), after federal EV incentives had ended earlier in 2025.

Provincially, British Columbia remained Canada’s leader with an 18.7% ZEV share, down slightly from 19.0% in Q1. Quebec edged higher from 17.6% to 17.8%. Ontario remained unchanged at 8.2%, recording 17,142 ZEVs out of 208,445 total new vehicle registrations.

Source: Statistics Canada

The results mark the third consecutive quarter in which ZEVs — which Statistics Canada defines as BEVs and PHEVs — accounted for more than one in 10 new vehicle registrations nationwide.

For comparison, Canada’s ZEV market had fallen sharply during 2025, even as hybrids gained ground.

data.title: SpaceX Moves to Stop Disclosure of $16.8B Terafab Project Documents in Texas
data.description:
SpaceX has gone to court in Texas to block the release of documents related to its Terafab facility. The company claims general accessibility will reveal sensitive information, putting the project at risk.

Elon Musk’s SpaceX is building a gigantic $16.5 billion chip factory in Grimes County. The company, however, wants to keep some aspects of the project secret. In its application suing the Attorney General and county, SpaceX wants to deter two public records requests seeking ‘sensitive’ information on costs, staffing, land acquisition, and technical details.

In the lawsuit before the Travis County District Court, SpaceX argues it competes in many markets. As such, some of the company’s deals “are competitively sensitive: their disclosure would reveal SpaceX’s costs, plans and negotiating strategy to competitors and to every other jurisdiction with which SpaceX negotiates.”

Local resident Vanessa Burzynski submitted a public records request in May under the Texas Public Information Act. Fellow Grimes County resident Marie Egyed filed their own request in June. Both of them want details of SpaceX’s communications with the county.

SpaceX approached the courts after AG Ken Paxton approved the release of some of the requested documents.

Terafab will produce semiconductors for autonomous vehicles, humanoid robots like Optimus, and extra-terrestrial data centers. Upon completion, the complex will cover 100 million square feet, making it the world’s largest building, according to Musk. It will employ more than 3,000 people.

The Terafab project enjoys county officials’ support and receives tax breaks. However, some residents oppose the development, arguing it would disrupt their rural lifestyle and crash property values.

data.title: U.S. Lawmaker Calls on NHTSA to Act on Sleeping Tesla Drivers
data.description:
A U.S. lawmaker is calling on federal regulators to take a closer look at Tesla’s driver monitoring safeguards following a growing number of videos showing drivers apparently asleep behind the wheel while using Autopilot or Full Self-Driving (FSD).

Representative Raja Krishnamoorthi, a Democrat from Illinois, sent a letter to U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy this week asking what the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is doing to address potential misuse of Tesla’s driver-assistance systems.

The letter follows an NBC News investigation that identified 43 videos appearing to show people asleep behind the wheel of moving Teslas, including 17 posted this year.

Krishnamoorthi argues regulators need to determine whether Tesla has sufficient safeguards against foreseeable misuse.

“FSD requires continuous human supervision, yet the message appears to encourage use of the system precisely when the vehicle has detected that the driver may be less capable,” Krishnamoorthi wrote, referring to Tesla’s “Drowsiness detected. Stay focused with FSD” message.

Similar incidents piling up in B.C.

While Krishnamoorthi’s concerns are directed at U.S. regulators, Canada has seen its own string of incidents, particularly in British Columbia.

At least five separate cases involving allegedly sleeping or significantly distracted Tesla drivers have surfaced in B.C. this year.

In March, police ticketed a Model Y driver who allegedly appeared asleep on Highway 1 in Coquitlam. In July, another driver was ticketed after police spotted them reading documents while using FSD in West Kelowna. That same month, video emerged of a Tesla driver apparently asleep while travelling between Golden and Revelstoke.

Two more incidents were revealed earlier this month. A Maple Ridge woman received a $368 ticket after witnesses allegedly recorded her sleeping behind the wheel on Highway 1 in North Vancouver, while another Tesla driver was ticketed after a B.C. Highway Patrol officer allegedly found him asleep during morning rush hour in Langley.

Krishnamoorthi has asked NHTSA to explain whether it considers the growing collection of sleeping-driver videos evidence of a broader safety problem and how effective Tesla’s driver-monitoring safeguards are at preventing misuse.
